questions.title: Does 5 U.S.C. § 1216(a)(3) create a mandatory duty for OSC to investigate FOIA withholdings, or is it discretionary?
questions.question_body: In the opinion, the district court held that § 1216(a)(3) does not limit OSC’s power, but the appellate court says the decision to investigate is discretionary. I'm confused about the statutory language: the section says OSC "shall … conduct an investigation" of arbitrary or capricious FOIA withholdings. Does the word "shall" impose an obligatory duty, or can the agency still decline investigation under its discretion? How have courts interpreted this provision in prior cases?

questions.title: What is the proper test for procedural‑injury standing under the “relaxed” standard, and why did the D.C. Circuit reject AFL’s claim?
questions.question_body: The opinion cites cases like *Center for Law & Education v. Department of Education* and *Fla. Audubon Society v. Bentsen* for a relaxed standing analysis when a procedural right is violated. What are the elements a plaintiff must prove under that relaxed test, and how did AFL fail to meet them according to the court? Specifically, why was the alleged informational injury not enough?

questions.title: How does the causation/redressability analysis differ for informational injuries versus procedural injuries in Article III standing?
questions.question_body: The court discusses both an informational injury (failure to get FOIA records) and a procedural injury (failure to receive OSC investigation notices). It finds both lacking causation and redressability, but I'm unclear on the standards applied to each type of injury. What is the distinction between the two analyses, and why can’t a court’s order compelling OSC to investigate satisfy either requirement?

questions.title: Why can the Supreme Court’s *Heckler v. Chaney* doctrine prevent a court from ordering an agency to exercise its enforcement discretion?
questions.question_body: The opinion references *Heckler v. Chaney* to explain why OSC’s discretion cannot be compelled. Could someone explain the scope of the Heckler doctrine, especially in the context of an agency’s decision whether to investigate alleged violations? Does it apply even when the statute appears to impose a mandatory duty?

questions.title: What is the relationship between FOIA’s § 552(a)(4)(F)(i) enforcement provision and OSC’s statutory authority under §§ 1214‑1216?
questions.question_body: The opinion distinguishes between the FOIA trigger for OSC action (the three predicates) and the separate authority under § 1216. How do these provisions interact? If the FOIA trigger is not met, can OSC still act under § 1216, or does the FOIA provision effectively pre‑empt OSC’s ability to investigate?

questions.title: Is an organization like America First Legal entitled to ‘informational standing’ under *Zivotofsky* or *Ake v. Oklahoma* doctrines?
questions.question_body: AFL argues it has an informational injury because it is denied notices and information that a statute would provide. How have courts treated informational standing claims by non‑individuals (e.g., NGOs or foundations) when the statute does not expressly grant a right to receive that information? Does *Zivotofsky* apply to organizational plaintiffs?

questions.title: What procedural steps are required when a district court dismisses a case for lack of standing after a supplemental briefing order?
questions.question_body: The appellate court vacated the district court’s judgment and remanded with instructions to dismiss for lack of subject‑matter jurisdiction. In practice, what does the district court need to do next? Does it issue a new order, a summary judgment, or a dismissal with prejudice? How does this affect any possibility of a future appeal?
